tagline: Downstream with the Corps of Discovery, Clarkston to the sea.
intro: The byway starts at Clarkston, where the Clearwater meets the Snake and the expedition first came into what is now Washington in October 1805. From there it follows the expedition west toward the sea, by Dayton and the Walla Walla vineyards to the Tri-Cities, then along the Oregon line through the Columbia River Gorge.

It runs about 572 miles in all. At Beacon Rock, the core of an ancient volcano, the journals first noted the pull of the tide. The road ends at Cape Disappointment, on the headlands where the Columbia meets the Pacific, which the Corps reached in 1805.
season: Usually open year-round; the state tourism office names spring and fall for mild weather.

moments.title: Dayton
moments.text: On the way home the Corps camped by Patit Creek. The town has kept the oldest working courthouse in Washington, finished in 1887 while it was still a territory, and a depot from 1881.

moments.title: Dismal Nitch
moments.text: A November storm in 1805 pinned the Corps in this cove for six days. "A feeling person would be distressed by our situation," Clark wrote. It is a rest stop now.

moments.title: Cape Disappointment
moments.text: The Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center stands on the cliffs 200 feet above the surf, in a park that also holds two lighthouses and the Civil War batteries of the old fort.
